theory.title: Describing a memorable first experience
theory.explanation: Para contar una experiencia concreta que ocurrió en un momento terminado, usamos past simple: I performed on stage last year. Usamos past continuous para describir lo que estaba ocurriendo alrededor de ese momento: I was waiting backstage when my name was called. When suele introducir el acontecimiento que interrumpe; while introduce una acción en progreso. Ordenamos la historia con at first, then, suddenly, as soon as, fortunately y in the end. Los adjetivos describen cómo nos sentíamos (I was nervous) o cómo era la situación (It was exciting).
theory.tip: Distingue la emoción de quien habla y la característica de la situación: I was frightened (yo tenía miedo), pero The ride was frightening (la atracción daba miedo).

patterns.label: Past simple: completed events
patterns.pattern: Subject + past verb; usa un tiempo pasado terminado.
examples: I tried surfing last summer.
We arrived at the station at eight.

patterns.label: Past continuous: background action
patterns.pattern: Was/were + verb-ing para una acción en progreso en el pasado.
examples: I was waiting outside.
They were talking when I arrived.

patterns.label: When: interrupting event
examples: I was taking a photo when it started to rain.
She was crossing the road when she saw her friend.

patterns.label: While: two actions in progress
patterns.pattern: While + past continuous, past continuous/past simple según el contexto.
examples: While I was getting ready, my phone rang.
While we were walking, we were talking.

patterns.label: Sequence: at first, then, finally
patterns.pattern: Usa conectores para que el oyente siga el orden.
examples: At first, I felt nervous. Then I relaxed. Finally, I enjoyed it.
First we checked the map; after that, we set off.

patterns.label: Suddenly and unexpectedly
patterns.pattern: Coloca suddenly o unexpectedly antes del hecho inesperado.
examples: Suddenly, the lights went out.
Unexpectedly, my name was announced.

patterns.label: Adjective: -ed feelings
patterns.pattern: -ed describe cómo se siente una persona.
examples: I was excited.
They felt disappointed.

patterns.label: Adjective: -ing qualities
patterns.pattern: -ing describe el efecto o la característica de algo.
examples: The trip was exciting.
It was a frightening experience.

patterns.label: As soon as
patterns.pattern: As soon as + past simple para indicar que algo ocurrió inmediatamente después.
examples: As soon as I arrived, I called my family.
As soon as the music started, everyone danced.

patterns.label: In the end
patterns.pattern: In the end introduce el resultado final de una experiencia.
examples: In the end, everything went well.
I was worried, but in the end I enjoyed the show.

content.passage: The first time I performed in front of an audience was at my school festival. I was thirteen and I had practised the guitar for weeks. On the day, the hall was crowded and I was feeling nervous while my friends were finding their seats. Just before the music started, one of my strings broke. For a moment, I wanted to leave the stage. Fortunately, my teacher brought me another guitar. As soon as I began to play, I stopped thinking about the audience. I made one small mistake, but I carried on. In the end, everyone clapped and I felt proud. It was not a perfect performance, but it taught me that I could overcome a difficult moment.

items.prompt: Describe the first time you travelled somewhere without your family. How did you feel?
items.modelAnswer: The first time I travelled without my family was when I was sixteen. I was nervous at first, but I became more confident during the trip.

items.prompt: Talk about a time when something unexpected happened.
items.modelAnswer: One day I was walking to class when it suddenly started to snow. I was surprised, but everyone was excited.

items.prompt: Describe your first day at a new school or job.
items.modelAnswer: On my first day, I didn't know anyone. I felt embarrassed at first, but a friendly classmate helped me.

items.prompt: Tell a story about a time you overcame a fear.
items.modelAnswer: I used to be afraid of speaking in public. I practised a lot, and eventually I gave a short presentation.

items.prompt: Describe a memorable celebration you attended for the first time.
items.modelAnswer: I went to a local festival for the first time last year. It was crowded and exciting, and I met many new people.

items.prompt: Talk about a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
items.modelAnswer: I once took the wrong train by accident. I felt worried, but I asked for help and learned to check the signs carefully.

items.prompt: Describe a moment when you felt proud of yourself.
items.modelAnswer: I felt proud when I finished my first long-distance race. I was tired, but I knew my preparation had helped.

items.prompt: Tell a story using 'while' and 'when'.
items.modelAnswer: While I was waiting for the bus, I met an old friend. We were talking when the bus finally arrived.

items.prompt: Describe an experience that turned out better than you expected.
items.modelAnswer: I was worried about my first music lesson, but it turned out to be great. The teacher was patient and I enjoyed it.

items.prompt: Tell a two-minute story about a first experience you will never forget.
items.modelAnswer: The first time I performed on stage was unforgettable. I was nervous while I was waiting, but as soon as I started, I felt more confident.

content.audioTranscript: Mia: Do you remember your first day at the climbing club? Alex: Yes! I was really nervous because I had never climbed before. Mia: What happened when you arrived? Alex: I was putting on my shoes when the instructor came over to help me. Mia: Were you frightened? Alex: A little. The wall looked very high, and the room was crowded. Mia: Did you give it a try? Alex: Yes. As soon as I started, I felt more confident. I slipped once, but fortunately I was wearing a safety harness. Mia: How did you feel in the end? Alex: Proud. It turned out to be a memorable afternoon, and now I look forward to going every week.
